question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's entrenched position as CCP General Secretary, Central Military Commission chairman, and president underpins the 95.5% trader consensus against removal before 2027. Term limits were eliminated in 2018, enabling extended tenure, while repeated military purges through early 2026—including senior PLA figures—have reinforced loyalty structures rather than eroding them. Xi has remained visibly active in 2026, issuing New Year messages, advancing diplomatic engagement, and directing defense modernization ahead of the PLA's 2027 centenary and the next Party Congress. This continuity aligns with historical patterns of consolidated one-man rule. Low-probability shifts could still arise from sudden health events, elite fractures, or unanticipated policy reversals, though no verified indicators currently point to such outcomes.
